simple.meaning: עֲיָם (ʻăyâm) is a Hebrew word meaning “probably meaning strength.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: עֲיָם (H5868) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Isaiah 11:15, with occurrences in Isaiah, Hosea.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲיָם (H5868) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in עֲיָם (H5868) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: עֲיָם (ʻăyâm) / H5868 is traced through Isaiah 11:15, Hosea 10:10 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H5868. ayam [ עֲיָם ] noun [masculine] dubious, possibly glow (Arabic , to thirst , thirst, internal heat ), si vera lectio (so Du; on form compare Nö ZMG xxxvii (1883), 526 ); — construct רוּחוֺ בֵּעְיָם Isa 11:15 , read perhaps בְּעֹצֶם (so apparently Vrss) Thes Luzz Krochm Che Gu Kau Gr Perles Anal. 52 .

occurrences.englishText: Yahweh will utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea; and with his scorching wind he will wave his hand over the River, and will split it into seven streams, and cause men to march over in sandals.
When it is my desire, I will chastise them;
